component.name: LSIW Control
component.summary: Configure how Windows programs run on Linux

description.p: LSIW (Linux Subsystem for Improved Wine) runs Windows x86-64 programs on Linux with its own engine: its own loader for Windows executables and its own implementations of the Windows system libraries. Wine is used only as a fallback for programs the engine cannot run yet.
LSIW Control is its settings app. With it you can:

ul.li: Choose where each Windows folder lives on Linux: Documents, AppData, Program Files, the Windows folder, Temp and every other folder variable Windows migration tools recognise
See the Windows path programs use for each folder: the whole Linux file system is the C: drive, and other disks appear as folders on it instead of new drive letters
Pick the engine that runs Windows programs: LSIW's own, Wine, or an automatic choice per program

description.p: Programs start with Proton again: prefixes Proton stopped on with "FileNotFoundError: tracked_files" are repaired. Steam installed by Debian's and Ubuntu's steam-installer is found, and the false "Steam is not installed" warning is gone.

LSIW keeps track of how long each program of the library runs: play time, launches and when it was last played, saved while it runs so crashes lose almost nothing. The Programs page can show the library as a Grid, a List or Details with sortable columns, and remembers the choice.

Any folder can be a drive of its own (D:, E:, ...) for LSIW's engine, Wine and Proton. LSIW checks for new releases once a day (this can be turned off) and LSIW Control can download, verify and install them. Releases now come with online and offline installers.
The C: drive is the hidden folder ~/.cdrive by default. An existing ~/c_drive moves there once and ~/c_drive becomes a link to it, so prefixes and shortcuts keep working.

LSIW shortcuts (.lwlnk): a Desktop shortcut button on the Programs page makes a file that starts the program with its settings when double-clicked, and shows the program's icon in file managers. Programs can have an icon of their own.

One shared prefix for every program and game under Wine and Proton, Steam games included; a C: drive folder you choose; a library of programs with their own engine, prefix, DXVK, VKD3D, arguments, environment, MangoHud and shortcuts; and a custom default engine with up to three fallbacks.
LSIW checks the Wine prefix before each program and installs .NET (Wine Mono) or Wine's services when they are missing, so installers such as Discord's work even when the first download failed.
Windows shortcuts (.lnk) open with LSIW, and the Create New menu has "Link to Windows Application...". The Wine prefix now has Wine's Windows services and .NET (Wine Mono), so more installers work.
Setting up the Wine prefix no longer fails with a crash of wine-preloader: Wine 11.20 is skipped, and a Wine build that crashes is replaced by the release before it.
The Proton list on the Engine page shows LSIW's version of every Proton. Setting up the Wine prefix works without 32-bit libraries.

Download Proton-CachyOS, DW-Proton, Proton-GE RTSP, Proton-Tkg, Proton-EM and Proton-Wineland from the Download Proton menu. Each one, and Proton 3.7 to 6.3, Hotfix and Proton Next, gets an LSIW twin in Steam.
Windows folders default to your home folder: ~/Windows, ~/Program Files, ~/ProgramData, and your profile is your home folder. Old locations are moved once.
The window can be made small: pages scroll and wrap. Downloaded Wine builds are named x86_64.

Every Proton in Steam's list, including Valve's versions that are not installed yet, gets an LSIW twin (LSIW Proton Stable, LSIW Proton Experimental, LSIW Proton 11.0-2, ...). GE-Proton downloads pick the build for this processor.
Choose the Wine and Proton versions, download GE-Proton and Wine builds, and add LSIW Proton to Steam from the new Steam integration page. Every engine uses the folders chosen here.
First release: the native engine for 64-bit console programs, the single C: drive, relocatable Windows folders, the Wine fallback and this settings app.
